This confirms macOS is not treating `pages.sandboxes.sandman` as absolute. It is appending your normal search domain:

```text
pages.sandboxes.sandman.tc42.uk
```

That is why only the trailing-dot form works.

For now, use:

```bash
pages.sandboxes.sandman.
```

The app-side DNS is fine; the macOS client behavior is the problem. I would not rely on a single-label private suffix like `sandman` for non-trailing-dot lookups on macOS.

Best durable fix: make the Sandcastle DNS suffix a real multi-label private domain, for example:

```bash
SANDCASTLE_NAME=sandman.internal
```

or better add a dedicated DNS suffix env var like:

```bash
SANDCASTLE_DNS_SUFFIX=sandman.internal
```

Then records become:

```text
pages.sandboxes.sandman.internal
test.p4.sandman.internal
```

macOS is much less likely to append `tc42.uk` to those, and `/etc/resolver/sandman.internal` will match cleanly.

I can patch this properly by adding `SANDCASTLE_DNS_SUFFIX`, keeping `SANDCASTLE_NAME` as fallback, and updating the CLI resolver install to write `search_order 1`.
